samples.summary: Deleted comment that marked `api-keys create` output as a one-time raw secret
samples.evidence: The diff removes `// Never suppress output — the raw key is shown only once` above the `output(res.data, opts.format)` call in `api-keys create`. Behaviour is unchanged (the call previously passed `quiet=false` explicitly and now `output()` can no longer be suppressed at all — verified `packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:26`, and the backend only returns the plaintext key from `create`, `packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.service.ts:36`, never from `list`, ibid. :46-54). The loss is documentational: that comment was the only in-code marker that this particular stdout write carries a plaintext credential (`wfb_…`, generated at api-key.service.ts:16) that lands in shell history/CI logs. Nothing exploitable follows from the deletion; re-stating the secret-handling note at the call site keeps the sensitivity visible to the next editor.

samples.summary: `outputError` now unconditionally echoes server-supplied and filesystem-derived error text to stderr, with no suppression path
samples.evidence: `outputError` no longer honours `--quiet` (formatter.ts:52-58), so every failure message is written to stderr regardless of flags. Some messages are attacker/server-influenced or environment-revealing: `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:42` throws `new Error(msg ?? 'HTTP ' + res.status)` where `msg` is taken verbatim from the remote response body (`res.data.error.message`), and import/export paths surface local file paths. A malicious or compromised server can therefore guarantee arbitrary text of its choosing reaches the operator's stderr and CI logs, where previously `--quiet` gave a way to drop it. Mitigations I confirmed: the payload goes through `JSON.stringify` (formatter.ts:54-56), which escapes all C0 control characters, so ANSI/OSC terminal-escape injection is not reachable by this path, and the emitted envelope carries no credential — no error message in the CLI interpolates `config.apiKey`/`accessToken` (grepped `apiKey|api-key|API key` and every `new Error(` in packages/cli/src). Impact is limited to log/terminal information disclosure of server-controlled strings and local paths; I could not build a stronger chain.

samples.summary: Result body (including remote-controlled cell/document content) is now printed for every invocation with no suppression path, in non-escaping formats
samples.evidence: `output()` now always `console.log(format(data, fmt))` (formatter.ts:26-28). For `--format table`/`csv` the body is emitted without JSON escaping (`packages/cli/src/output/table.ts`, `csv.ts`), so raw C0/ANSI sequences stored in a document or cell by another workspace member are written straight to the operator's terminal. This is pre-existing for the default (non-quiet) path — the change only removes `--quiet` as an accidental escape hatch — so it is not introduced here; flagging it as hardening because the change makes the unescaped write unconditional. A `format`-level control-character strip for table/csv would close it.
